subproblem.title: C¹ regularity of a graph carrying decaying tilt-excess (proof of Simon 5.5.2)
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 1, k ≥ 0, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} any set, R = (M, θ, ξ_R) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n; ξ_R = R.orient is its orientation, and ξ below denotes a point) with μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), W ⊆ U open, κ ∈ ℝ, H : ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ^{n+k} μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |H(x)| ≤ κ for all x, such that R.firstVariation X = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ for every C¹ compactly supported X : ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ^{n+k} with tsupport X ⊆ W. Let ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{n+k} be linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w, f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ with |f(v) − f(w)| ≤ ¼|v − w| for all v, w and f(0) = 0, z ∈ ℝ^{n+k}, a > 0, s₀ > 0 and K ∈ ℝ (K may be negative; K⁺ := max{K, 0}), such that B_a(z) ⊆ W, spt μ ∩ B_a(z) = F ∩ B_a(z) with F := {z + ιv + ι'f(v) : v ∈ ℝⁿ}, and for every ξ ∈ spt μ ∩ B_a(z) there is an n-dimensional subspace S with ∫_{B_s(ξ)} |p_x − p_S|² dμ ≤ K⁺s^{n+1} = max{K, 0}·s^{n+1} for all s ∈ (0, s₀]. This bound is exactly the Lean bound ENNReal.ofReal (K * s ^ (n + 1)): for s > 0, ENNReal.ofReal(K s^{n+1}) = max{K s^{n+1}, 0} = max{K, 0}·s^{n+1}, so for K < 0 the hypothesis says that these integrals vanish, exactly as for K = 0 (the bound is not the possibly negative real number K s^{n+1}). Then f is C¹ on the open ball B̆_{a/2}(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f (ball 0 (a/2))). Here p_x is the orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n M x, p_x^⊥ := I − p_x, p_S the orthogonal projection onto a subspace S, |A|² := Σ_i |Ae_i|² the Hilbert–Schmidt norm (the Lean sum over EuclideanSpace.single i 1), B_t(y) the closed ball, and integrals of nonnegative functions are lower Lebesgue integrals in [0, ∞] (Lean ∫⁻ of ENNReal.ofReal).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ), 0 < n → ∀ (U W : Set (Euclid (n + k))) (R : IMRep U n) (H : Euclid (n + k) → Euclid (n + k)) (κ : ℝ) (ι : Euclid n →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (ι' : Euclid k →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (f : Euclid n → Euclid k) (z : Euclid (n + k)) (a s₀ K : ℝ), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → AEStronglyMeasurable H R.measure → (∀ x, ‖H x‖ ≤ κ) → (∀ X : Euclid (n + k) → Euclid (n + k), ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ W → R.firstVariation X = -∫ x, inner ℝ (X x) (H x) ∂R.measure) → (∀ v w, inner ℝ (ι v) (ι' w) = 0) → (∀ v w, ‖f v - f w‖ ≤ 1 / 4 * ‖v - w‖) → f 0 = 0 → 0 < a → 0 < s₀ → closedBall z a ⊆ W → R.measure.support ∩ closedBall z a = range (fun v => z + ι v + ι' (f v)) ∩ closedBall z a → (∀ ξ ∈ R.measure.support ∩ closedBall z a, ∃ S : Submodule ℝ (Euclid (n + k)), Module.finrank ℝ S = n ∧ ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ s₀ → ∫⁻ x in closedBall ξ s, ENNReal.ofReal (∑ i : Fin (n + k), ‖(approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) - S.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))‖ ^ 2) ∂R.measure ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (K * s ^ (n + 1))) → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f (ball (0 : Euclid n) (a / 2))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Sibling map (dependency key — frozen Lean declaration — labels used below): tangent_projection_measurable — Submission.dorag_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm (x ↦ p_x is AE-strongly measurable for μ = R.measure); monotonicity — Submission.dorag_monotonicity_density ((M1) and (M2) are the first and second conjuncts of its first conclusion ∀ y s t, 0 < s → s < t → closedBall y t ⊆ W → (M1) ∧ (M2); (D) is its second conclusion ∀ y ∈ spt μ, ∀ t > 0, closedBall y t ⊆ W → ∫_{B_t(y)}F_y dμ + ω_n ≤ e^{κt}t^{−n}μ(B_t(y))); support_null — Submission.dorag_support_sdiff_carrier_null (Hⁿ((spt μ ∩ W) ∖ M) = 0); graph_tangent — Submission.dorag_lipschitz_graph_approxTangent (tangent planes along a Lipschitz graph).
Source: parent proof Parts 8.5–8.8 (Simon Ch. 5, proof of Theorem 5.2, (9)–(11) and the final paragraph, with the parent's corrections), stated for a general radius a, scale s₀ and decay constant K (the parent uses a = σ₀/8, s₀ = σ₀/2, K = C₁₇E₀/σ₀ ≥ 0, c₀ = 1/4; an arbitrary real K is allowed here and is handled through K⁺ := max{K, 0}, see (D_K) below). Conventions: E := ℝ^{n+k}; B_t(y) closed ball, B̆_t(y) open ball; Bⁿ_t(v), B̆ⁿ_t(v) balls in ℝⁿ; M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M, Hⁿ := μHE[n], Lⁿ Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ; ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞), used as a positive real number; p_x := projection onto T_xM := approxTangentPlane n M x; |A|² Hilbert–Schmidt, ‖A‖ ≤ |A| operator norm. Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'f(v), F := Φ(ℝⁿ); for a linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ, graph A := {ιw + ι'Aw : w ∈ ℝⁿ} = LinearMap.range(ι + ι'∘A), and p_A := its orthogonal projection. Siblings used: monotonicity ((D)), support_null, graph_tangent, tangent_projection_measurable.

The decay hypothesis (D_K). Put K⁺ := max{K, 0} ≥ 0. For s > 0 we have s^{n+1} > 0, hence ENNReal.ofReal(K s^{n+1}) = max{K s^{n+1}, 0} = K⁺s^{n+1} (if K ≥ 0 both sides equal K·s^{n+1}; if K < 0 both sides are 0). Therefore the last hypothesis of the statement, whose Lean form is ∫⁻_{B_s(ξ)} ofReal(|p_x − p_S|²) dμ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (K * s ^ (n + 1)), says exactly:
 (D_K) for every ξ ∈ spt μ ∩ B_a(z) there is an n-dimensional subspace S with ∫_{B_s(ξ)}|p_x − p_S|²dμ ≤ K⁺s^{n+1} for every s ∈ (0, s₀].
Only (D_K), with the nonnegative constant K⁺, is used below; for K < 0 it says that these integrals vanish, which is the case K⁺ = 0 and needs no separate treatment. The label (D) below always refers to the sibling monotonicity's density bound, never to (D_K).

Preliminaries. (P1) κ ≥ 0 since κ ≥ ‖H(x)‖. (P2) For compact Γ ⊆ W, μ(Γ) = ∫_{M∩Γ}θ dHⁿ < ∞ (IMRep.locallyIntegrable_mult, Γ ⊆ W ⊆ U) and Hⁿ(M ∩ Γ) ≤ μ(Γ) (θ ≥ 1 on M; we write Γ for compact sets because K is the decay constant); if B_t(y) ⊆ W then B_{t'}(y) ⊆ W for some t' > t. (P3) For μ-a.e. x: x ∈ M and T_xM is an n-dimensional approximate tangent plane of M at x (IMRep.orients, the definition of approxTangentPlane and uniqueness HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), so p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-plane and trace p_x = n; x ↦ p_x is μ-AE-strongly measurable (tangent_projection_measurable). (P4) (MC) denotes the hypothesis R.firstVariation X = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ for every C¹ compactly supported X with tsupport X ⊆ W; for such X, div_M X(x) = trace(p_x∘DX(x)) (Lean tangentialDivergence) is bounded, μ-measurable (P3) and supported in a compact subset of W, hence μ-integrable (P2), and R.firstVariation X = ∫_Mθ div_M X dHⁿ = ∫div_M X dμ; so (MC) reads ∫div_M X dμ = −∫⟨X, H⟩dμ. (P5) μ(E ∖ M) = 0 and μ(E ∖ spt μ) = 0; μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M and Hⁿ⌞M ≤ μ, so μ-null and Hⁿ⌞M-null sets coincide.
0. Geometry of Φ. As ι, ι' are isometries with orthogonal ranges (and n + k = dim E, so E = ι(ℝⁿ) ⊕ ι'(ℝᵏ)), |Φ(v) − Φ(v')|² = |v − v'|² + |f(v) − f(v')|²; with Lip f ≤ 1/4 and f(0) = 0: |v − v'| ≤ |Φ(v) − Φ(v')| ≤ (17/16)^{1/2}|v − v'|, |Φ(v) − z| ≤ (17/16)^{1/2}|v| < 1.04|v|, Φ is injective, and Lⁿ(Z) ≤ Hⁿ(Φ(Z)) for Z ⊆ ℝⁿ (Φ^{−1} is 1-Lipschitz on F). By Rademacher's theorem f is differentiable Lⁿ-a.e., with ‖Df‖ ≤ 1/4 there; J(v) := (det(I + Df(v)ᵀDf(v)))^{1/2} ≥ 1 is the area Jacobian of Φ. Let Ω' := B̆ⁿ_{4a/5}(0); for v ∈ Ω', |Φ(v) − z| < 1.04·0.8a < a, so Φ(v) ∈ F ∩ B_a(z) = spt μ ∩ B_a(z) ⊆ W.
1. Hⁿ⌞(F ∩ B_a(z)) ≤ μ. F ∩ B_a(z) ⊆ spt μ ∩ W, and Hⁿ((spt μ ∩ W) ∖ M) = 0 by support_null; θ ≥ 1 on M. So for Borel Y, Hⁿ(Y ∩ F ∩ B_a(z)) ≤ Hⁿ(Y ∩ M) ≤ ∫_{Y∩M}θ dHⁿ = μ(Y). Consequently, if N ⊆ E is μ-null (or Hⁿ-null) then Lⁿ({v ∈ Ω' : Φ(v) ∈ N}) ≤ Hⁿ(N ∩ F ∩ B_a(z)) = 0.
2. Lower density. For ξ ∈ spt μ ∩ B_a(z) ⊆ W and s > 0 small enough that B_s(ξ) ⊆ W and κs ≤ ln 2 (κ ≥ 0), monotonicity (D) gives μ(B_s(ξ)) ≥ e^{−κs}ω_nsⁿ ≥ ½ω_nsⁿ.
3. Tangent planes along the graph (parent 8.5; Simon (10)). Let G be the set of v ∈ Ω' such that, with ξ_v := Φ(v): (i) f is differentiable at v; (ii) ξ_v ∈ M and T_{ξ_v}M = graph Df(v) (in Lean: approxTangentPlane n M ξ_v = LinearMap.range(ι + ι'∘Df(v))); (iii) ξ_v is a μ-Lebesgue point of x ↦ p_x: lim_{s↓0} μ(B_s(ξ_v))^{−1}∫_{B_s(ξ_v)}|p_x − p_{ξ_v}|²dμ = 0. Then Lⁿ(Ω' ∖ G) = 0: (i) fails on an Lⁿ-null set (Rademacher); (ii) fails, for v ∈ Ω' with (i), only if Φ(v) lies in the Hⁿ-null set (spt μ ∩ W) ∖ M (support_null) or in the Hⁿ-null exceptional set of graph_tangent (applied with the base point z in place of graph_tangent's parameter a, Lipschitz constant L := 1/4, the given ι, ι', f, and W), so by 1 on an Lⁿ-null set; (iii) fails only if Φ(v) lies in the μ-null set of non-Lebesgue points in B_a(z) of the bounded μ-measurable map x ↦ p_x (tangent_projection_measurable; fix a' > a with B_{a'}(z) ⊆ W, possible as B_a(z) is compact and W open, and apply Lebesgue's differentiation theorem for the finite Borel measure μ⌞B̆_{a'}(z) on E (Besicovitch; Mathlib ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub), whose small balls about points of B_a(z) coincide with those of μ), so by 1 on an Lⁿ-null set.
 For v ∈ G let S_v be the n-plane given by (D_K) at ξ_v ∈ spt μ ∩ B_a(z): ∫_{B_s(ξ_v)}|p_x − p_{S_v}|²dμ ≤ K⁺s^{n+1} for 0 < s ≤ s₀. Then p_{S_v} = p_{graph Df(v)}: for small s > 0 (s ≤ s₀ and as in 2), averaging the pointwise inequality |p_{ξ_v} − p_{S_v}|² ≤ 2|p_x − p_{ξ_v}|² + 2|p_x − p_{S_v}|² over B_s(ξ_v) with respect to μ gives |p_{ξ_v} − p_{S_v}|² ≤ 2μ(B_s(ξ_v))^{−1}∫_{B_s(ξ_v)}|p_x − p_{ξ_v}|²dμ + 2μ(B_s(ξ_v))^{−1}K⁺s^{n+1}, where the first term → 0 by (iii) and the second is ≤ 4K⁺s/ω_n → 0 by 2; so p_{S_v} = p_{ξ_v} = p_{graph Df(v)} by (ii).
4. Projections of graphs (parent 8.6). For linear A₁, A₂ : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ with ‖A₁‖, ‖A₂‖ ≤ 1/4: |A₁ − A₂| ≤ 2|p_{A₁} − p_{A₂}|. Proof: for u ∈ ℝⁿ, p_A(ιu) = ιw + ι'Aw where w minimizes |u − w|² + |Aw|², i.e. w = (I + AᵀA)^{−1}u; so ι'*p_Aι = A(I + AᵀA)^{−1}. Then ι'*(p_{A₁} − p_{A₂})ι = (A₁ − A₂)Y₁ + A₂Y₁(A₂ᵀA₂ − A₁ᵀA₁)Y₂ with Y_i := (I + A_iᵀA_i)^{−1}, ‖Y_i‖ ≤ 1, ‖Y_i^{−1}‖ ≤ 1 + 1/16. Using |XY| ≤ ‖X‖|Y|, |XY| ≤ |X|‖Y‖ and |X| ≤ |XY|‖Y^{−1}‖: |(A₁ − A₂)Y₁| ≥ (16/17)|A₁ − A₂|, and |A₂Y₁(A₂ᵀ(A₂ − A₁) + (A₂ − A₁)ᵀA₁)Y₂| ≤ (1/4)(2·(1/4))|A₁ − A₂| = (1/8)|A₁ − A₂|. Hence |ι'*(p_{A₁} − p_{A₂})ι| ≥ (16/17 − 1/8)|A₁ − A₂| ≥ ½|A₁ − A₂|, and |ι'*(p_{A₁} − p_{A₂})ι| ≤ |p_{A₁} − p_{A₂}| (ι, ι' are isometries).
5. Campanato estimate (parent 8.7; Simon (11)). Put s₁ := min{s₀/2, a/8}. Let v ∈ G with |v| < a/2 and 0 < s ≤ s₁. For v' ∈ Bⁿ_s(v): |v'| < a/2 + a/8 < 4a/5 (so v' ∈ Ω'), and |Φ(v') − ξ_v| ≤ 1.04|v' − v| < 2s; also |ξ_v − z| < 1.04·a/2 < 0.53a, so B_{2s}(ξ_v) ⊆ B_a(z) (2s ≤ a/4). For a.e. v' ∈ Bⁿ_s(v) we have v' ∈ G, hence p_{Φ(v')} = p_{Df(v')} (3(ii)). By 4 (‖Df‖ ≤ 1/4), 3 (p_{S_v} = p_{Df(v)}), J ≥ 1, the area formula for the injective Lipschitz map Φ (Simon Ch. 2, 3.5; library injective_area_formula_lipschitz), Φ(Bⁿ_s(v)) ⊆ F ∩ B_{2s}(ξ_v), 1, and (D_K) at ξ_v with radius 2s ≤ s₀ (the integrand x ↦ |p_x − p_{S_v}|² is μ-a.e.-measurable by (P3), hence a.e.-measurable for Hⁿ⌞(F ∩ B_a(z)) ≤ μ; the library's weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn accepts any nonnegative weight):
 ∫_{Bⁿ_s(v)}|Df(v') − Df(v)|²dv' ≤ 4∫_{Bⁿ_s(v)}|p_{Φ(v')} − p_{S_v}|²J(v')dv' = 4∫_{Φ(Bⁿ_s(v))}|p_x − p_{S_v}|²dHⁿ ≤ 4∫_{F∩B_{2s}(ξ_v)}|p_x − p_{S_v}|²dHⁿ ≤ 4∫_{B_{2s}(ξ_v)}|p_x − p_{S_v}|²dμ ≤ 4K⁺(2s)^{n+1}.
6. Hölder continuity of Df on G (parent 8.7). Let v₁, v₂ ∈ G with |v₁|, |v₂| < a/2 and 0 < s := |v₁ − v₂| ≤ s₁, and m := (v₁ + v₂)/2. Then Bⁿ_{s/2}(m) ⊆ Bⁿ_s(v₁) ∩ Bⁿ_s(v₂), and averaging |Df(v₁) − Df(v₂)|² ≤ 2|Df(v') − Df(v₁)|² + 2|Df(v') − Df(v₂)|² over v' ∈ Bⁿ_{s/2}(m) gives, by 5 applied at v₁ and at v₂ with radius s, |Df(v₁) − Df(v₂)|² ≤ (ω_n(s/2)ⁿ)^{−1}·2·2·4K⁺(2s)^{n+1} = C₁₉²K⁺s with C₁₉² := 2^{2n+5}/ω_n. So |Df(v₁) − Df(v₂)| ≤ C₁₉(K⁺|v₁ − v₂|)^{1/2} for v₁, v₂ ∈ G ∩ B̆ⁿ_{a/2} with |v₁ − v₂| ≤ s₁ (K⁺ ≥ 0, so the square root is defined).
7. C¹ regularity (parent 8.8). Let Ω := B̆ⁿ_{a/2}(0). G ∩ Ω has full measure in Ω, hence is dense in Ω, and by 6 the restriction of Df to G ∩ Ω is uniformly continuous; let g : Ω → Hom(ℝⁿ, ℝᵏ) be its unique continuous extension (uniformly continuous, with g = Df on G ∩ Ω). As f is Lipschitz, its distributional derivative is the a.e. derivative Df, so Df = g Lⁿ-a.e. on Ω. For a standard mollifier ϱ_t and Ω_t := {v ∈ Ω : dist(v, ℝⁿ ∖ Ω) > t}, the smooth maps f_t := f ∗ ϱ_t satisfy Df_t = (Df) ∗ ϱ_t = g ∗ ϱ_t on Ω_t (for Lipschitz f, D(f ∗ ϱ_t)h = lim_{τ→0}((f(· + τh) − f)/τ) ∗ ϱ_t = (Df h) ∗ ϱ_t by dominated convergence: the difference quotients are bounded by Lip f·|h| and converge a.e. to Df·h by Rademacher's theorem); g ∗ ϱ_t → g locally uniformly on Ω (g uniformly continuous), and f_t → f uniformly (f continuous, Lipschitz). If f_t → f pointwise and Df_t → g locally uniformly on an open set with g continuous, then f is C¹ there with Df = g (fundamental theorem of calculus on segments: f_t(v + h) − f_t(v) = ∫₀¹Df_t(v + τh)h dτ → ∫₀¹g(v + τh)h dτ for [v, v + h] ⊆ Ω, whence f(v + h) − f(v) − g(v)h = o(|h|)). Therefore f is C¹ on Ω = ball (0 : Euclid n) (a/2), i.e. ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f (ball 0 (a/2)). ∎
proof_key_steps: Read the Lean decay bound ENNReal.ofReal (K * s ^ (n + 1)) as ∫_{B_s(ξ)}|p_x − p_S|² ≤ K⁺s^{n+1} with K⁺ := max{K, 0} ≥ 0 (s > 0); for K < 0 the integrals vanish.
Geometry of Φ; Hⁿ⌞(F ∩ B_a(z)) ≤ μ by support_null and θ ≥ 1.
For a.e. v: T_{Φ(v)}M = graph Df(v) (graph_tangent), and the Lebesgue point property forces S_v = graph Df(v).
Campanato estimate ∫_{Bⁿ_s(v)}|Df − Df(v)|² ≤ 4K⁺(2s)^{n+1}, via the area formula.
Hölder bound |Df(v₁) − Df(v₂)| ≤ C₁₉(K⁺|v₁ − v₂|)^{1/2} on a full-measure set, and its continuous extension g.
Mollification: Df_t = g ∗ ϱ_t → g locally uniformly, so f is C¹ on B̆ⁿ_{a/2}.

audit.reason: The revised prose correctly interprets ENNReal.ofReal using K⁺, including negative K. Tangent identification, the projection estimate for slopes at most 1/4, Campanato control and mollification prove C¹ regularity on exactly ball 0 (a/2). The proof uses only its stated dependencies.
